answer: Each agent may propose a trade, but only trades backed by a deposit enter the market. After delivery, the buyer can challenge fraud; an independent verifier checks signed receipts, and a failed challenge forfeits the seller’s deposit to the buyer and verifier. A new identity must lock fresh funds, so splitting one dishonest operation across many names multiplies the capital at risk instead of multiplying influence for free. The voyage can be long, but each lantern-lit ledge still has a toll.
